name: Draft London Plan consultation
fact: Draft London Plan consultation is open from July to 15 October 2026 and covers housing, jobs, transport, environment and public space, looking ahead roughly 20–25 years.
gate: Draft consultation policy is not an adopted plan, site allocation, permission or exact parcel relation.

name: Draft London Plan 2026
fact: Published 16 July 2026 as a draft Spatial Development Strategy with chapters on land, housing, economy, resilience and place-based approaches.
gate: Draft strategy must not be treated as adopted policy or parcel certainty.

name: Draft London Plan homes chapter
fact: Published 16 July 2026; chapter includes policies on increasing housing stock, affordable housing, build to rent and specialist accommodation.
gate: Strategic housing policy is not site allocation, capacity confirmation or delivery evidence for a parcel.

name: Draft London Plan economy chapter
fact: Published 16 July 2026; chapter includes employment space, industrial land, data centres, visitor infrastructure and other economic policies.
gate: Draft economic policy does not establish an occupier, consent, infrastructure capacity or parcel development probability.

name: Draft London Plan place visions
fact: Published 16 July 2026; draft policies include Brownfield First Opportunity Areas, CAZ, town centres, strategic economic clusters/corridors and industrial land supporting housing growth.
gate: Place-based draft policies require exact adopted geography and site relation before promotion.

name: Draft London Plan land use chapter
fact: Published 16 July 2026; chapter addresses spatial strategy, site capacity, utilities capacity/connectivity/resilience and sustainable transport for growth.
gate: Policy intent is not evidence of actual utility headroom, transport delivery or parcel capacity.

name: Draft London Plan resilience chapter
fact: Published 16 July 2026; chapter includes energy efficiency, low-carbon heat, whole-life carbon, heat risk, flood risk/drainage and biodiversity.
gate: Draft environmental policy does not clear site-specific environmental constraints or confirm development capacity.

name: Mayor decision MD3515 on Draft London Plan
fact: Mayor decision signed 9 July and published 16 July 2026 approved the Draft London Plan for formal statutory consultation.
gate: Formal consultation approval is not adoption of the plan or a site-specific planning decision.

name: GLA Draft London Plan engagement portal
fact: Official engagement portal summarises the draft plan and consultation closing 15 October 2026, covering land, homes, economy, resilience and place visions.
gate: Engagement material supports current-status verification only; it is not adopted policy evidence.

name: New local plan-making system roadmap
fact: Updated 19 May 2026; MHCLG roadmap sets out tools, gateways, evidence, guidance, open-data support and funding for faster new-style local plans.
gate: Implementation roadmap does not establish an authority's adopted spatial strategy or site allocation.

name: Gateway 1 local plan guidance
fact: Published 23 June 2026; Gateway 1 starts the structured 30-month local-plan preparation process after readiness and self-assessment steps.
gate: Gateway status is procedural and cannot be converted into parcel allocation or timing certainty.

name: Gateway 2 local plan guidance
fact: Published 22 June 2026; Gateway 2 guidance describes the assessment stage for new-style local plans before later plan preparation steps.
gate: Gateway progress is not adoption, allocation or development permission.

name: Gateway 3 local plan guidance
fact: Published 22 June 2026; Gateway 3 is the final mandatory gateway assessing readiness to submit a local plan for examination within the 30-month process.
gate: Readiness for examination does not make draft allocations adopted or deliverable.

name: New-style local plan examination process
fact: Published 18 June 2026; Planning Inspectorate states the new plan-making system began in March 2026 and both legacy and new systems operate during the 2026 transition.
gate: System status alone does not prove any individual plan or site has passed examination.

name: New-style local plan guidance collection
fact: Published 18 June 2026; official collection centralises guidance and procedure for plans prepared under the 2026 regulations.
gate: Guidance collection is procedural context, not site evidence.

name: Local plan housing land supply evidence collection
fact: Published 1 June 2026; Planning Inspectorate templates support evidence for each residential allocation and other sites assumed to contribute to five-year supply.
gate: Templates do not prove that a site is deliverable; authority evidence and examination findings remain required.

name: Local plan public engagement guidance
fact: Published 15 April 2026; guidance sets scoping, proposed-content and proposed-plan consultations, including minimum consultation periods and evidence disclosure.
gate: Consultation stage or representation does not equal policy adoption or parcel allocation.

name: Spatial development strategies geography consultation
fact: Published 12 February 2026; MHCLG sought views on geographies for Spatial Development Strategies ahead of strategic-planning implementation.
gate: Consulted geographies are not automatically final statutory SDS boundaries.

name: Spatial development strategies detailed consultation
fact: Detailed 2026 paper explains proposed SDS geographies, strategic planning boards and preparatory work before statutory arrangements are finalised.
gate: Proposed geographies and preparatory activity cannot be treated as an adopted spatial strategy.

name: Consulting Secretary of State on planning decisions
fact: Published 23 March 2026; consultation covers proposed Secretary of State consultation requirements for certain commercial, nuclear and defence-zone planning decisions.
gate: Consultation proposals are not final directions except where separately enacted.

name: Planning consultation directions collection
fact: Published 31 March 2026; collection identifies Town and Country Planning Consultation Directions currently in force in England.
gate: Direction coverage is a procedural trigger and does not establish planning outcome for a site.

name: Town and Country Planning Consultation Direction 2026
fact: Published 31 March 2026 as a Direction under the Development Management Procedure Order 2015.
gate: Direction status does not itself grant or refuse development permission.

name: Streamlining infrastructure planning consultation
fact: Updated 3 July 2026; consultation covers pre-application, acceptance, pre-examination, examination and NSIP service reforms.
gate: Process reform cannot be treated as consent, programme funding or parcel benefit.

name: NSIP decision-making stage guidance
fact: Published 3 July 2026; guidance explains statutory and non-statutory expectations for the decision-making stage of Development Consent Order applications.
gate: Process guidance is not evidence that any individual NSIP has been approved.

name: National Infrastructure Planning Guidance Portal
fact: Updated 3 July 2026; portal is the central source for current national infrastructure planning guidance and identifies July 2026 replacement guidance.
gate: Guidance availability does not establish scheme consent or delivery.

name: NSIP linear projects application advice
fact: Planning Inspectorate advice was updated 14 July 2026 and covers route design, construction, land rights and environmental assessment for linear NSIPs.
gate: Application-preparation advice does not establish route approval or property impact.

name: Data centres essential services factsheet
fact: Updated 30 June 2026; government states qualifying data centres will be designated essential services and notes data centres were designated critical national infrastructure in 2024.
gate: CNI status is sector context, not evidence of planning permission, grid capacity or investment at a parcel.

name: Data-centre NSIP biodiversity gain statement
fact: Published 2 June and updated 16 June 2026; statement sets BNG requirements for data-centre NSIPs, mandatory for NSIPs from 2 November 2026.
gate: BNG framework does not identify approved data-centre sites or clear ecology constraints.

name: AI Growth Zones collection
fact: Official collection tracks AI Growth Zone announcements and guidance, including Oxfordshire and North East in England and programme policy updates.
gate: Programme collection is not exact site boundary, power availability or development consent evidence.

name: Delivering AI Growth Zones policy
fact: Policy paper sets out energy, planning, skills and investor-support reforms intended to accelerate AI data-centre capacity through AI Growth Zones.
gate: Policy support does not prove an individual data-centre project is viable, connected or consented.

name: AI Growth Zones applications guidance
fact: Guidance invites public authorities and industry to propose AI Growth Zones and emphasises power access, planning support, investment and high-skilled jobs.
gate: Application eligibility does not establish designation or development probability for a site.

name: AI Opportunities Action Plan one year on
fact: Published 29 January 2026; government reports 38 of 50 actions met and identifies five AI Growth Zones plus expanded public compute as delivered foundation measures.
gate: National delivery progress is not a parcel-level development signal.

name: North East AI Growth Zone skills and growth update
fact: Published 12 May 2026; update links the North East AI Growth Zone to billions of pounds of investment and new local skills programmes.
gate: Regional investment and skills activity require exact site, investor and planning evidence before parcel promotion.

name: UKAEA strategy 2026-2030
fact: UKAEA strategy includes a September 2026 target to deliver the government's first AI Growth Zone at Culham and begin operation of the Sunrise fusion-dedicated AI supercomputer.
gate: Programme milestone does not establish surrounding parcel development, power headroom or planning status.

name: Heathrow expansion consultation launch
fact: Published 18 June 2026; government launched consultation on the framework for future third-runway decisions and says expansion could support over 60,000 new local jobs.
gate: Consultation and economic estimates are not planning permission or proof of parcel uplift.

name: Heathrow Expansion NPS factsheet
fact: Published 18 June 2026; factsheet explains the draft HENPS and makes clear it is not planning permission for a third runway.
gate: Draft policy framework cannot be represented as consent, construction commitment or property-level impact.

name: About the draft Heathrow Expansion NPS
fact: Published 18 June 2026; government states the draft HENPS will guide future development-consent assessment if designated, subject to air quality, climate, economic-growth and noise tests.
gate: Draft NPS status and policy tests are not consent or site-specific growth proof.

name: Clean Power 2030 technical annex
fact: Technical annex estimates Clean Power 2030 could require around £40bn average annual investment from 2025-2030, including generation and transmission investment.
gate: National investment scenarios do not identify local grid headroom, project consent or parcel benefit.

name: Clean Power 2030 main report
fact: Main report says Great Britain needs around twice as much new transmission infrastructure by 2030 as delivered in the prior decade and links network expansion to economic growth.
gate: System need does not identify exact reinforcement timing or connection capacity for a development.

name: Ofgem ED3 grid investment methodology
fact: Published 21 May 2026; Ofgem set methodology for 2028-33 distribution-network investment plans while noting uncertainty in scale, timing and location of electrification.
gate: Price-control methodology is not local capacity or a connection offer.

name: Great British Energy clean energy and jobs
fact: Government describes Great British Energy's mission to invest in, develop and own clean-energy projects while supporting jobs, growth and supply chains.
gate: Corporate mission is not evidence of a funded project affecting a specific parcel.

name: Government clean energy investment milestone
fact: Published 24 June 2026; government reports more than £100bn of private clean-energy investment announcements since taking office.
gate: Aggregated announcements do not establish individual project financial close, construction or parcel-level uplift.
